evidence: Read the current page and the correctness theorem; the one-positive-meridian-per-under-arc and crossing-conjugacy conventions match the KT-20 group use.
Read the current exterior, positive meridian/preferred longitude, and homology/longitude carriers. The latter retains full AC, which dependent statements preserve.

Read the twisted-chain and Fox-boundary carriers. Their right-action/row convention, full-AC branch, and presentation-complex limitation are recorded; no geometric character-variety theorem is inferred from them.

The satellite and JSJ definitions were inspected. The current JSJ theorem proof explicitly leaves uniqueness step 3.2 unresolved, so the required page interface cannot supply a proved satellite/JSJ trichotomy.

The page and current Batch-73 theorem are present. The theorem retains the full multi-cusp statement but leaves the local deformation neighborhood and general rigidity proof unresolved; it is not treated as a proved filling supplier.
The required page edge is preserved. Its current Batch-97 analytic instanton and KHI detector carriers have provenance.proof not-supplied; the pair does not treat them as proved logical premises.
The B companion declares its A page as a same-batch prerequisite. Both authored inventories are present and their direct item links remain in the batch manifest.

The irreducibility proof uses this current smooth Schoenflies theorem. Its full statement and proof were inspected; the theorem itself depends on a substantial smooth surface-normal-form and isotopy-extension chain that is not reconciled here.

The boundary-incompressibility proof closes by the genus-zero criterion. Its complete current proof was inspected; it in turn uses the smooth chart/normal-form and isotopy-extension chain that remains under prerequisite audit.

The current deformation lemma explicitly says the Mostow supplier has provenance.proof not-supplied and only covers knot exteriors with one cusp, while this use needs arbitrary finite k-cusped manifolds.
The theorem’s proof cites the multi-cusp deformation lemma but that carrier leaves the simultaneous peripheral-logarithm rank and neighborhood-existence argument unresolved.

Requires the Nielsen covering theorem for the specific pi1-injective map of compact surfaces arising from the lift of the nonseparating surface to F×R; the map must be homotopic to a finite-sheeted covering so degree can be compared with the longitude boundary class. Proposed placement: surface-theory prerequisite before this lemma.

Requires an isotopy theorem for the constructed incompressible surfaces in the fibered knot exterior, respecting the fixed boundary data. Proposed placement: surface-theory prerequisite before this lemma.

Requires a proof that the two affine eigenline incidence charts, defined over Q, have projected reduced Zariski-closed locus whose complex points give the scalar extension of a radical Q-ideal. Proposed placement: A-page algebraic-geometric helper before this lemma.

Requires the generic SL2 matrix invariant theorem that simultaneous-conjugation invariants are generated by traces of words, followed by a verified passage to the relator quotient. Proposed placement: A-page invariant-theory module before this lemma.

Requires separate irreducible-character conjugacy and reducible semisimplification/rational-descent theorems under the stated SL2(C) hypotheses. Proposed placement: A-page character-variety module before this model.

Requires a proved categorical-quotient restriction map, lift to the peripheral eigenvalue torus, elimination of all trace/eigenline variables, and separation of reducible L=1 from nonabelian curve components while excluding isolated points as curve factors. Proposed placement: A-page elimination theorem before this lemma.

Requires a rational descent statement for the rank-fixed Fox/boundary kernel-line bundle from representation patches to the character component, with compatibility across minor charts and conjugation. Proposed placement: A-page character-variety module before this lemma.

Requires the valuation-to-tree action and essential-surface construction for an ideal point of the peripheral eigenvalue curve, with the meridian/longitude sign and reciprocal convention checked against the Newton edge. Proposed placement: A-page Culler–Shalen module before this theorem.

Requires the ideal-point tree construction plus a proof the edge surface is strict, including the argument excluding the fiber case via normality of the fiber subgroup. Proposed placement: A-page Culler–Shalen strict-surface module before this theorem.
